text.p: -- Lehman Bros analyst Tim Wallace said in a research note that he initiated coverage of Pegasus Communications Corp with a buy recommendation.
-- Direct broadcast satellite, which for Pegasus is the reselling of Hughes Electronics Corp's DirecTV, and television segmants will drive growth, according to Wallace.
-- Shares added 1/2 to 11-3/4 in morning Nasdaq trade.

-- "Pegasus operates in three businesses: DBS, braodcast TV and cable. Higher penetration rates from PGTV's rural DirecTV franchises and significant operating leverage from its FOX/UPN TV affiliates should drive strong cash flow growth over the next 12-18 months," he said.

-- "Pegasus is the largest DirecTV franchisee in the U.S. with exclusive selling rights for the service to approximately one million rural households. Management intends to increase its DirecTV 'footprint' to 2.5 million to three million rural households over the next few years. With penetration rates for rural DirecTV estimated 15 percent to 2002, Pegasus could potentially 'own' 450,000 households," Wallace wrote.
